Name: hexapod
Description: Common Hexagellies live in temperature waters around the world and can tolerate a wide range of temperatures. But, they are slow growing and take a long time to mature.

Name: gelgi
Description: Common Gelgi photosynthesize using chlorophyll, giving them their characteristic green color.

Name: yelloo
Description: Common Yelloo form massive schools in the wild during the spring making the sea appear bright yellow.

Name: hexapod tropical
Description: Tropical Hexagellies like to bask in warm, sunlight-filled waters. They don't tolerate cold conditions, but when they are warm, they can grow and reproduce very rapidly.

Name: gelgi tropical
Description: Tropical Gelgi have a second row of spines, making them resemble rays of sunlight.

Name: yelloo tropical
Description: The brightly-colored Tropical Yelloo put on elaborate displays to confuse their predators.

Name: hexapod arctic
Description: Cold-loving (Arctic) Hexagellies resemble snowflakes leading to their common name "sea crystals."

Name: gelgi arctic
Description: Unlike other subspecies of Gelgi, the Arctic Gelgi subspecies has rigid spines to protect themselves from predators.

Name: yelloo arctic
Description: Arctic Yelloo are very pale to help them blend into their environment. Like Hexagellies, they are photosynthetic and get their energy from the sun.

Name: shelpik
Description: Shells of the Common Sheplik become redder as they grow older. Their color makes them a popular pet in captivity.

Name: grabbler
Description: After Common Grabblers hatch, they seek out the shell of a Sheplik to protect their delicate tails.

Name: cyplo
Description: The Common Cyplo is known for its bright orange color and single eye. Their winks are considered good luck.

Name: shelpik tropical
Description: The Tropical Sheplik is also known as the royal sheplik because their shiny shells resemble a golden crown.

Name: grabbler tropical
Description: The elongated claws of the Tropical Grabbler allow them to reach into many tight places other grabblers cannot.

Name: cyplo tropical
Description: Tropical Cyplos have highly effective spines to help protect themselves from predators.

Name: shelpik arctic
Description: Arctic Sheplik are very slow moving and resilient to cold. It is said that they can hibernate for months in the cold.

Name: grabbler arctic
Description: Arctic Grabblers are fast walkers and can use air chambers in their shells to float.

Name: cyplo arctic
Description: Arctic Cyplos thrive in cold water where they can often be found playing with small bits of ice.

Name: rooda
Description: The Common Rooda are apex predators that hunt using their sharp heads to impale their prey.

Name: sploof
Description: Common Sploof are thought to be highly intelligent. Lab studies have shown that they are able to solve simple puzzles.

Name: silu
Description: The Common Silu-Silu have voracious appetites, eating anything that happens to be in front of them.

Name: rooda tropical
Description: The colorful Tropical Rooda can contort their bodies into strange shapes to hypnotize their prey before eating them.

Name: sploof tropical
Description: Tropical Sploof are very playful, they love blowing small objects such as  sand and shells around with their jets.

Name: silu tropical
Description: The huge whiskers of the Tropical Silu-Silu allow them to detect any changes in the water around them.

Name: rooda arctic
Description: Arctic Rooda are built for speed with their streamlined bodies. They are the fastest swimmers in the ocean.

Name: sploof arctic
Description: Arctic Sploof are known to sometimes jump out of the water to roll around in snow on land. The reason is unknown.

Name: silu arctic
Description: Arctic Silu-Silu have very small eyes that are less developed than most other fish. They use their whiskers to feel around.
